I reviewed 40 resumes last month.
None of the 7 that got interviews opened with a skills list.

33 of the 40 did open with one. Six lines or more.

A long skills list tells the reader nothing. Every candidate writes the same words. "Team player." "Detail oriented." "Hard worker." The reader scrolls past before the second line.

The 7 resumes that got interviews started differently. Each one opened with one line about a result.

What those lines had in common:
• They said what the person changed
• They gave one result a stranger could picture
• They left the skills for the job entries below

A busy reader gives you a few seconds. That is all. A skills list spends those seconds on words everyone else also wrote. A result spends them on proof.

I now tell every job seeker the same thing.

Cut the skills list from the top. Write one line about a result you got. Then start your first job entry.

You do not need new skills. You need a better first line.

Skills still matter. Put them inside each job entry, next to the work that shows them. The reader then sees the skill and the proof in the same glance, and does not have to take your word for it.

The first line decides if the second one gets read.
